why.detail: Many people keep the heat off so they never fall behind, so the alternative line 'I can't afford to keep my home warm' makes the difference clear. Heating is going without warmth to avoid the bill; Utility bills is being behind on the bills already, which can include water.

current.name: Heating
current.line: I can't afford to heat my home.

proposed.name: Utility bills
proposed.line: I'm behind on my power or water bill.

side.name: Internet
side.line: I can't get decent internet.

side.name: Transport
side.line: I struggle to get where I need to go.

why.detail: Both can cut people off from work and services, but nobody would confuse a slow connection with having no ride. Internet is not being able to get online at a decent speed or price; Transport is not being able to get to places.

current.name: Internet
current.line: I can't get decent internet.

proposed.name: Transport
proposed.line: I struggle to get where I need to go.

side.name: Safety
side.line: I don't feel safe where I live.

side.name: Crime
side.line: I don't feel safe from crime and violence.

why.detail: Not feeling safe where I live and not feeling safe from crime are the same pain seen from the personal and societal pages, so they stay two pains linked across pages.

current.name: Safety
current.line: I don't feel safe where I live.

proposed.name: Crime
proposed.line: I don't feel safe from crime and violence.

side.name: Safety
side.line: I don't feel safe where I live.

side.name: Safety at home
side.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.

why.detail: The two need very different help, and the alternative name Unsafe area keeps them from both reading as Safety. Safety is danger in the neighborhood; Safety at home is danger from someone in my own life.

current.name: Safety
current.line: I don't feel safe where I live.

proposed.name: Safety at home
proposed.line: I don't feel safe with someone in my life.
